text.linkedin:
The design rule I check every Wrapbox decision against:

If Wrapbox fails, crashes or gets removed, the agent must end up less capable. Never more. And the failure must be visible.

It sounds obvious. In my view it isn't how many guardrails behave: the policy service times out, and the call goes through.

So in wrapboxd, the on-device runtime I'm building for AI coding agents:

→ Decisions happen locally, from a cached ruleset. The network is never on the decision path.
→ A kernel sandbox (macOS Seatbelt) sits under the agent. A denied read of .env or ~/.ssh fails with EPERM even if the agent never asks the hook.
→ Every decision and every kernel denial becomes a signed receipt in a hash chain the server can verify.

It has honest limits. Seatbelt can't filter network traffic by domain, only localhost or everything. Path rules match paths, not file contents. I'd rather say that up front than oversell it.

When the guardrails around your agents fail, do they fail open or closed? Have you actually tested it?

#BuildInPublic #AISecurity #AIAgents
